principle: Translate reference principles into client-native systems; do not clone assets or trade dress.

doac_practitioner.source: Cameron Macklin — trailer animation process for The Diary of a CEO
supported_points: An 8-second animation was storyboarded before production.
Custom B-roll can be built from scratch when the story needs it.
Storyboarding provides direction and narrative clarity.
Story and narrative take priority over tech/design spectacle.
doac_practitioner.use_in_system: Every <=9s cinematic beat receives a storyboard/state plan before generation.

supported_points: Explainer format combines depth with strong design.
Animation, texture, personality and curiosity are part of the explanatory language.
Customization matters; the visual system is not a universal skin.
vox_official.use_in_system: VOX_EDITORIAL uses diagrams/type/photo/data only when each element advances the explanation.

supported_points: Explainer logic can be adapted to social-first shorter formats.
vox_official.use_in_system: Short-form treatment keeps explanatory logic without compressing into generic kinetic text.

supported_points: Motion is design with time, rhythm, pacing and transformation.
Real-world physics is a reference for believable motion.
Easing, anticipation, overshoot, follow-through, hold and settle form a useful motion grammar.
Transitions connect beats of a story.
Flashy motion for motion's sake is weaker than intentional communication.
figma_official_2026.use_in_system: Every animation prompt encodes acceleration/deceleration/settle and semantic trigger.

supported_points: Motion can be systematized as components/variables rather than one-off effects.
Timing, easing and keyframes need inspectable handoff.
figma_official_2026.use_in_system: Treatment families are reusable motion system values, not random effect names.

supported_points: Reference images can guide generated video.
Native vertical generation is supported.
1080p/4K upscaling is available in the workflow.
google_flow_official_2026.use_in_system: START/MIDDLE/END frames and client reference ingredients are first-class production assets.

supported_points: Multiple reference images can control characters, objects and style.
Flow offers more precise editing and higher-quality outputs.
google_flow_official_2026.use_in_system: Prompt packs distinguish reference roles: character, object, environment, style.

supported_points: Omni Flash in Flow supports multimodal creative iteration.
Real-world references can be mixed with generated content.
google_flow_official_2026.use_in_system: The handoff prompt explicitly instructs reference-grounded edits rather than fresh scene invention.

observations: Extreme close-ups treat fruit, botanical tissue, droplets, cells and biomaterials as hero landscapes.
Useful qualities are microtexture, translucency, wetness, natural asymmetry, controlled specular highlights and shallow depth.
observed_visual_archetypes.do_not_infer: The system should not default to brains, cells, ginger or microbiome; these are examples of quality/material scale.

observations: Microscopy, petri dishes, molecules, plants and lab devices are paired with large negative space and restrained typography.
Scientific imagery often acts as the main photographic field rather than a small decorative icon.
Phone/app screens sit inside botanical/scientific environments with depth and material contrast.
Data/UI cards use hierarchy, soft layering and limited accent colors.
Single hero objects or macro surfaces carry the visual; typography is large but leaves the object legible.
Black/white/off-white backgrounds and controlled accent color create premium clarity.
Fine lines, nodes, pill labels, simple charts and circular relationships can overlay photographs without turning them into HUD sci-fi.
Dark scenes use luminous glass/data cards and selective neon rather than filling the frame with random glow.
Depth comes from material, occlusion and lighting, not only blur.
Everyday objects become mechanisms: paper, doors, chains, keyboards, clocks, chess, threads, cards, blocks.
The object must map to a spoken concept or process.
When people appear, action is readable: typing, writing, inspecting, testing, holding, walking, reviewing.
Pose, hand-object contact, gaze and perspective must agree.

camera: Intentional focal feel rather than generic wide shot.
Macro, portrait, top-down, product hero and documentary framing are chosen by narrative function.
lighting: Motivated key light, controlled fill, natural rolloff, local contrast and depth separation.
materials: Liquids need surface tension and coherent droplets.
composition: Text safe zones planned before generation.
realism: No fake UI or pseudo-scientific data presented as evidence.

moka_brand_reference.rule: Moka identity stays scientific, human, precise and professional; avoid generic wellness and generic sci-fi.

safe_replication_policy: Do not request exact recreation of a Vox, DOAC or third-party visual.
Use client palette, type and brand assets as identity layer.
Reference assets can guide material/camera/style but must produce a new scene.
Label conceptual scientific renders as illustrative when not source evidence.

audit_notes.doac_status: Practitioner/process reference, not an official DOAC normative source. Use only for storyboard/story-over-tech production principles.
audit_notes.reference_pdf_policy: Extract materials/camera/texture/quality grammar, not recurring object subjects.
